title: Cross-SDK conformance linter and invocation adapter with progressive stream recovery
creator: Asha Patel
description: Goal: ship a multi-language SDK feature set that (1) statically and at-runtime validates function/tool schemas against a lightweight conformance linter, (2) provides a small runtime invocation adapter that enforces safe coercions and idempotency tokens, and (3) improves streaming ergonomics by enabling progressive recovery and partial-result fallbacks when downstream tool calls fail. This ticket covers design, implementation, tests and rollout across Python/TypeScript/Go SDKs.
acceptance_criteria: A conformance-linter CLI runs as a dev dependency and flags schema mismatches and unsupported types with clear error codes
SDK runtime adapters perform pre-invocation validation and emit structured telemetry for every validation and retry decision
Streaming call paths can resume from the last emitted checkpoint for partial tool responses and continue token streaming without full restart
End-to-end examples included in each SDK repo demonstrating: schema linting, safe coercion, idempotent retries, and progressive stream recovery
Performance: validation + lightweight adapter adds < 2ms median overhead to a cold function call in each SDK on our benchmark harness
Docs and migration guide published; migration tests for existing users pass in CI
implementation_notes: Conformance linter: small TypeScript core that parses JSON Schema-like function specs and enforces a restricted subset (primitives, enums, arrays-of-primitives, structured objects up to 3 levels). Linter emits machine-readable diagnostics and suggested coercions

Runtime adapter: language-specific thin layer (Python/TS/Go) that accepts a function spec and incoming args, runs the linter in fast-mode, applies safe coercions (string->number, allow empty->null) when configured, and attaches an idempotency token header for retries

Streaming recovery: introduce a compact checkpoint framing inside streamed responses (checkpoint metadata + KV of last-processed-call), adapter keeps last-complete-checkpoint and can replay only missing segments to resume stream

Retry policy: progressive retries with three tiers: fast jittered short-backoff, durable backoff for transient infra, and fallback to model-only response when tool is unavailable. Each retry emits telemetry with outcome labels: recovered|degraded|failed
Telemetry: new event types: sdk.validation.error, sdk.validation.suggested_fix, sdk.invocation.retry, sdk.stream.checkpoint, sdk.invocation.fallback. Include token counts and timing buckets

Examples: produce 3 canonical examples per SDK repo: (a) statically lint + fix, (b) runtime coercion + idempotent retry after 409, (c) streaming tool that fails mid-stream and recovers from checkpoint
Interop: ensure TypeScript core can be consumed by Go/Python via prebuilt JSON diagnostics and a tiny language shim for runtime checks to avoid shipping full TypeScript runtime
testing_plan: Unit tests for linter rules (positive/negative fixtures across languages)
Fuzz tests: random malformed schemas and argument payloads to verify linter stability
Integration tests: end-to-end calls against a local test tool service that can simulate partial failures, dropped connections, 5xxs and delayed responses
Load test: benchmark median overhead and p95 with and without adapters on our standard invocation harness
Chaos scenarios: network partition between SDK and tool; ensure checkpoint resume within 30s for streaming workloads
Compatibility tests: verify existing customers' schema files still pass with 'strict:false' mode enabled
rollout_steps: Merge conformance linter to monorepo and publish npm package (internal alpha)
Publish language shims for Python and Go that call linter outputs and include runtime adapter
Publish Python/TS/Go SDK releases behind a feature flag: allow opt-in via SDK config
Run opt-in dogfood with 3 internal product teams for 2 weeks, gather telemetry and fix edgecases
Flip default to enabled in minor release after internal validation and docs complete
Announce migration guide and sample PRs in SDK repo READMEs
